how_we_lost: P3 (Giada Angels) killed us on round 13 (T51). P1 and P2 were already dead, and P3 had about 60 flying power and 80 life (lifelink). Muldrotha landed on round 6 and we drained P2 to 1 (P1 finished it), but three things went wrong. (1) On round 9 (T35) P3's Austere Command wiped Muldrotha, Vrock, Plaguecrafter, Strix and Apprentice, while Glen Elendra had sat in hand since round 7. (2) On the rebuild the pilot aimed resources and attacks at P1 and let P3's Exemplar of Light / Herald's Horn / Urza's Incubator / Seraph Sanctuary engine grow. (3) On round 12 (T45) the executor attacked P1 (2 life) into an untapped 13/13 Wight of the Reliquary, losing Muldrotha and Gray Merchant, and Galactus chapter I was then aimed at that Wight instead of Lyra. P3 hit us for 16 on T49 and for lethal on T51.
winnable_why: We were at 20+ life until round 12, Muldrotha was online from round 6, two opponents died around us, and the answers for P3 were in hand for turns: Glen Elendra, Twisted Embrace, Plaguecrafter recursion, Galactus, Dellian, Shriekmaw. Three plays would probably have left Muldrotha looping removal into a 1v1 against P3: Glen before Austere Command, the Plaguecrafter edict on the shrouded Exemplar on T39, and no suicidal attacks on T42/T45. It was not certain. P3's lifegain-counter snowball was strong, and we never drew Toxic Deluge or Pernicious Deed.

mistakes.what_happened: The memo's line was: Marionette Apprentice from the graveyard, then sacrifice Mishra's Bauble and Sakura-Tribe Elder for two Apprentice drains to kill P1 at 2, Concoction on Lyra, no attack. The executor cast Bauble and sacrificed it BEFORE Apprentice was on board (no drain), and Apprentice was never cast. It then OVERRULED Forge's 'don't attack' twice to send Muldrotha and Gray Merchant at P1, who had an untapped vigilant Wight of the Reliquary 13/13, Teval, 6+ untapped Plants and 4 Zombies. Wight blocked Muldrotha, and both of our creatures died.
mistakes.better_play: No attack. Apprentice first, then the Bauble/STE sacrifices (P1 dead), then Concoction on Lyra with Glen's U open.
mistakes.why: It lost the commander (the recast now cost 10), the Gray Merchant body, and the P1 kill. We had no engine for the final two rounds against P3's 40+ flying power.

mistakes.what_happened: After the escalation, the replanned memo said to cast The Coming of Galactus with chapter I on Lyra Dawnbringer (anthem plus lifelink on every Angel). The chapter I trigger took Forge's default target, P1's Wight of the Reliquary. P1 was at 2 life and the Wight had already done its damage.
mistakes.better_play: Chapter I on Lyra, as the memo said.
mistakes.why: Lyra's lifelink took P3 from 42 to 75 on the next swing and added +1/+1 to every attacker. That was 16 damage to us on T49 and left us at 4.

mistakes.what_happened: The T28 memo said to cast Glen Elendra 'next turn, before we go all-in'. With 8 mana on T32, the new memo went all-in on removal (Bauble, Embrace, Concoction, Relic) and dropped Glen. The executor then spent the remainder on Vrock (not in the memo) and skipped both Embrace and the Relic recast. On T35 P3 cast Austere Command (the dossier gives 40% Austere, 38% Farewell) and killed Muldrotha plus four creatures.
mistakes.better_play: Glen Elendra (4) plus Concoction on the worst threat, keeping U open. Glen counters Austere Command, and persist keeps the shield up for a second wipe.
mistakes.why: Muldrotha was the whole engine. Losing her set us back a full turn cycle and 2 tax, and it swept Vrock, Plaguecrafter, Strix and Apprentice. Caveat: the digest can't show whether the executor would have been offered the Glen activation on P3's turn.
mistakes.category: no protection for the engine / overextended into wipe

mistakes.what_happened: The memo said: Glen Elendra; Cabal Pit on Giada; then Plaguecrafter from the graveyard, so that P3, whose only other creature was Exemplar of Light shrouded by Lightning Greaves, must sacrifice Exemplar. The executor used the creature lane on Vrock and OVERRULED Forge to evoke Shriekmaw from hand. Shriekmaw's trigger took Forge's default target, a 1/2 Plant token. Glen stayed in hand again, and P1's Victimize resolved uncontested on T40.
mistakes.better_play: Pit on Giada, Plaguecrafter from the graveyard (P3 is forced to sacrifice Exemplar), Glen from hand with U open.
mistakes.why: Exemplar of Light was P3's card-draw and counter engine. It drew every turn and grew to 13/13, the base of the Angel army that killed us. Edicts are the deck's only way through Greaves shroud.

mistakes.what_happened: The escalation memo said: don't attack; Vrock's end-step trigger (Bauble and the fetch already left the battlefield) kills P1 at 2. The executor accepted Forge's attack with Muldrotha and Vrock into P1's board. Vrock died in that combat, so there was no end-step trigger, and P1 survived at 2 for two more rounds (and killed Muldrotha on T45).
mistakes.better_play: No attack. Keep Vrock home as the end-step drain and a flying blocker.
mistakes.why: It lost the drain engine and the P1 kill in one decision.

mistakes.what_happened: Twisted Embrace was never cast all game (held from T4 and finally discarded to Concoction). On T28 the memo's line was Embrace on Cryogen Relic to kill Baloth Prime. Instead the executor recast Strix and then OVERRULED Forge's 'hold' to sacrifice Relic for a stun counter with no target, which also removed the Embrace host. The same thing happened on T32: Bauble was sacrificed at once instead of carrying Embrace.
mistakes.better_play: Embrace on Relic or Bauble, killing Baloth Prime (T28) or The Gitrog Monster (T32).
mistakes.why: Baloth Prime made three more 4/4s, and Gitrog lived. The waste was repeated removal left in hand plus about 2 mana on a no-target stun.
mistakes.category: removal left in hand / wasted mana

strategy_assessment: The engine plan (Muldrotha looping Concoction, Plaguecrafter, Bauble, and Vrock/Apprentice/Gray drains) was right, and it worked well enough to help kill P2. The memos misread the table in two ways. Early, they ranked Hearthhull and Zuran Orb as threat #1 and held Boseiju for them all game, but Hearthhull was never cast. Late, they spent turns and combat trying to finish P1 at 2, even though P1's big board was mostly attacking P3. At this table Giada is the deck that wins long games: lifegain plus counters snowball, it runs about 1.8 wipes, and in this game it got hexproof from Metropolis Reformer. From round 8 on, the correct plan was: (a) once Muldrotha is online, keep Glen Elendra up every turn against Austere Command or Farewell; (b) spend the recurring lanes every turn on P3's engine pieces (Giada, Exemplar, Lyra, Harbinger), using the edict when Greaves shrouds; (c) never attack into untapped fatties, since the drains close the game. The executor also repeatedly accepted Forge plays that replaced the memo (Vrock on T32 and T39, Galactus' target on T45) and made two fatal attack decisions.
summary: We lost to P3's Angels on round 13 after controlling the early game and helping kill P2. The decisive errors were: no Glen Elendra shield before P3's Austere Command (T32/T35); Vrock plus Shriekmaw-on-a-Plant instead of the planned Plaguecrafter edict on Exemplar (T39); and two suicidal attacks at P1 (T42 lost Vrock, T45 lost Muldrotha and Gray Merchant into a 13/13), followed by Galactus hitting P1's Wight instead of Lyra. A strong pilot probably wins or at least goes deep into a 1v1.
